notes: The tutorial covers many circuits (LED, button, buzzer, traffic lights, PIR, ultrasonic, MCP3008, motors). The supplied circuit images show only the LDR + capacitor light-sensing circuit, so that is the graph built.

Pi is shown rotated 180 degrees. Red wire goes to the top-row pin at the right-hand end (pin 1, 3V3), green to the top row pin 7 (GPIO4, matching LightSensor(4)), black to the bottom-row pin 6 (GND). Pin 6 is assumed to be GND.1 in the catalogue.

The breadboard images show columns 1, 3 and 5. Red wire is in column 1, green in column 3, black in column 5. The LDR spans columns 1 and 3. The capacitor spans columns 3 (positive, long leg, same track as the LDR leg and GPIO4) and 5 (negative, to GND). Rows were chosen within the top half (a-e) of the strips. The LDR rows are approximate.
The manual lists a 1uF capacitor; the catalogue only has capacitor-10uf (polarized POS/NEG), so it is used with value=1uF.
Jumper leads are male-to-female: port a is the female end on the Pi header, port b is the male end in the breadboard.
